chunks: Design rule checks (DRC). The question: What are design rule checks (DRC)?

A design rule check, or DRC, is an automatic check that compares your board layout with a list of rules, such as the smallest gap between copper paths, the thinnest trace, and the smallest drill hole.
The rules come from what the factory can build and what your circuit needs. If the layout passes, it can be made. That does not prove the design is right.
Think of a spell checker. It underlines misspelled words, but it will happily accept a perfectly spelled sentence that says the wrong thing. DRC is the same.
It measures every gap and width quickly, and it never gets tired, but it cannot tell whether you wired the right pin to the right place.
DRC combines two rule sources (the fab's limits and your own electrical needs) with the layout.
A clean result is an input to release, not the conclusion; the right-hand box lists what DRC cannot cover.
Trace: a copper path on the board that carries a signal or power. Net: all the points that are wired together as one connection.
Clearance: the smallest allowed gap between copper of two different nets. Annular ring: the copper left around a drilled hole after the hole is made.
Fabricator: the factory that makes the bare board.
Say the fabricator can reliably make a 0. 1 mm gap and no smaller. You draw two traces from different nets only 0. 08 mm apart.
DRC flags them at once, because they might touch and connect two signals that must stay apart (a short). Now a hole. A pad 0. 6 mm wide with a 0. 3 mm drill has a ring of (0.
6 minus 0. 3) ÷ 2 = 0. 15 mm of copper around the hole. Drills wander a little and layers do not line up perfectly, so up to about 0. 1 mm can be lost, leaving as little as 0.
05 mm. So the factory's ring rule includes margin for this, and DRC flags any pad whose ring is smaller than the rule, telling you to enlarge it. That is the whole idea.

"DRC is an automated check of the PCB layout against rules: clearance between nets, minimum trace width, drill and annular ring, solder mask and silkscreen rules, board-edge distance and connectivity.
I set the rules from the fab's capability sheet plus my electrical needs, and run it after every routing session.
A clean DRC means it's manufacturable by those rules, not that it's correct, so I still need ERC, review and bring-up."
